'''Rimantas Šadžius''' (born 8 October 1960) is a Lithuanian politician and economist affiliated with the [[Social Democratic Party of Lithuania]]. He served as the [[Ministry of Finance (Lithuania)|Minister of Finance]] under Prime Minister [[Gintautas Paluckas]], a position he assumed on 12 December 2024. Šadžius has held the finance portfolio multiple times, having previously held it from 2007 to 2008 and from 2012 to 2016. He has also served as Acting Prime Minister from 4 August to 25 September.

Following the resignation of Prime Minister [[Gintautas Paluckas]] on 31 July 2025, President [[Gitanas Nausėda]] appointed Finance Minister Rimantas Šadžius as Acting [[Prime minister|Prime Minister]] on 4 August 2025. He led a caretaker government until the [[Seimas]] approved the formation of the [[Ruginienė Cabinet]] on 25 September 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sytas |first=Andrius |last2=Sytas |first2=Andrius |date=2025-08-04 |title=Lithuania's finance minister to lead caretaker government |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/lithuanias-finance-minister-lead-caretaker-government-2025-08-04/ |access-date=2025-08-07 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.reuters.com/world/lithuanias-parliament-approves-new-government-2025-09-25/|title= Ruginiene becomes Lithuania's prime minister, pledges more defence spending|first=Andrius|last=Sytas|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=2025-09-25|access-date=2025-09-26}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Vilnius]], Šadžius graduated from [[Vilnius University]] with a degree in chemistry before transitioning into public administration and economics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lrs.lt/sip/portal.show?p_r=8825&p_k=2&p_person_id=14256|title=Rimantas Šadžius - Member of the Seimas|website=LRS.lt|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

==Political career==
Šadžius began his political career in the Ministry of Finance, holding various senior roles before being appointed as Minister of Finance.

=== Minister of Finance ===
==== First Term (2007–2008) ====
Šadžius was first appointed Minister of Finance on 16 May 2007 under Prime Minister [[Gediminas Kirkilas]]. During this time, he worked on fiscal reforms and preparations for Lithuania's eventual adoption of the euro.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://finmin.lrv.lt/en/about-the-ministry/history/after-restoration-of-independence|title=History of the Ministry of Finance|website=finmin.lrv.lt|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

==== Second Term (2012–2016) ====
Šadžius returned to the Ministry of Finance in December 2012 under Prime Minister [[Algirdas Butkevičius]]. His second term focused on navigating Lithuania through the post-2008 financial crisis recovery, implementing tax reforms, and enhancing fiscal stability. During this period, he chaired the [[Party of European Socialists]]’ Finance Ministers Network, where he advocated for measures against corporate tax avoidance and promoted fiscal harmonization in the European Union.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pes.eu/oc/en/news-events/news/detail/PES-Finance-Ministers-call-for-ambitious-measures-to-tackle-corporate-tax-avoidance/|title=PES Finance Ministers Call for Ambitious Measures to Tackle Corporate Tax Avoidance|website=Party of European Socialists|date=25 May 2016|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

==== Current Term (2024–present) ====
Following the [[2024 Lithuanian parliamentary election]], Šadžius was nominated by Prime Minister [[Gintautas Paluckas]] to serve as Minister of Finance, succeeding [[Gintarė Skaistė]]. He took office on 12 December 2024 and has outlined priorities that include reducing income inequality, increasing public sector efficiency, and enhancing Lithuania's economic resilience amid global financial uncertainties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lrt.lt/naujienos/lietuvoje/2/2420859/rimantas-sadzius-named-minister-of-finance-in-paluckas-government|title=Rimantas Šadžius Named Minister of Finance in Paluckas Government|date=12 December 2024|website=LRT|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

In June 2025, Šadžius put forward his candidacy to become the president of the [[Eurogroup]], competing with fellow candidates [[Paschal Donohoe]] and [[Carlos Cuerpo]];<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eurogroup presidency: three ministers put forward their candidacies |url=https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2025/06/27/eurogroup-presidency-three-ministers-put-forward-their-candidacies/ |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=Consilium |language=en}}</ref><ref>Inti Landauro (27 June 2025), [https://www.reuters.com/en/spains-economy-minister-launches-bid-lead-eurogroup-2025-06-27/ Spain's economy minister launches bid to lead Eurogroup] ''[[Reuters]]''.</ref> shortly after, he withdrew his name from consideration, citing insufficient support.<ref>Gregorio Sorgi (7 July 2025), [https://www.politico.eu/article/breaking-spains-cuerpo-drops-out-of-eurogroup-presidency-race/ Ireland’s Donohoe holds on to Eurogroup presidency as challengers drop out] ''[[Politico Europe]]''.</ref>

In January 2026, the Lithuanian government submitted Šadžius as a candidate to succeed [[Luis de Guindos]] in the position of [[President of the European Central Bank#Vice Presidents|Vice-President of the European Central Bank]];<ref>Jan Strupczewski (9 January 2026), [https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/six-candidates-bid-replace-ecb-vice-president-de-guindos-eurogroup-2026-01-09/ Six candidates bid to replace ECB vice president de Guindos -Eurogroup] ''[[Reuters]]''.</ref><ref>[https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/01/09/statement-by-the-eurogroup-president-on-the-nominations-for-the-post-of-ecb-vice-president/ Statement by the Eurogroup President on the nominations for the post of ECB Vice-President] [[General Secretariat of the Council of the European Union]], press release of 9 January 2026.</ref> following a vote within the [[Eurogroup]], the role eventually went to [[Boris Vujčić]] instead.<ref>Paola Tamma (19 January 2026), [https://www.ft.com/content/25fa0397-70d3-47a0-85e8-eda2f495378d Croatian central bank governor elected ECB’s second-in-command] ''[[Financial Times]]''.</ref>

== Post-ministerial career ==
From 2016 to 2022, Šadžius served as the Lithuanian member of the [[European Court of Auditors]], where he focused on improving transparency and accountability in the management of EU financial programs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eca.europa.eu/ContentPagesDocuments/History/ECA_Members_since_1977.pdf |title=The Members of the European Court of Auditors since 1977
|website=eca.europa.eu|access-date=10 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eca.europa.eu/en/Pages/DocItem.aspx?did=43406|title=European Court of Auditors Annual Report 2016|website=eca.europa.eu|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

== Other activities ==
* [[European Investment Bank]] (EIB), Ex-Officio Member of the Board of Governors (2007–2008, 2012–2016, 2024–present)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eib.org/en/publications/annual-report-2007.htm|title=2007 Annual Report|publisher=European Investment Bank|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>
* [[International Monetary Fund]] (IMF), Ex-Officio Alternate Member of the Board of Governors (2007–2008, 2012–2016, 2024–present)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imf.org/en/Publications/Annual-Report/Issues/2016/12/31/IMF-Annual-Report-2016|title=IMF Annual Report 2016|website=imf.org|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Rimantas Šadžius is married and resides in Vilnius. He is an active supporter of cultural and educational initiatives aimed at fostering economic literacy among young people.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sadzius.lt|title=Official Website of Rimantas Šadžius|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>
